0.0.n: A personal pronoun commonly used by male speakers, softer than 俺.

0.1.n: Marks 僕 as the topic: the speaker is talking about himself.

0.2.n: Combines with 1年生 to specify the level of schooling.

0.3.n: Names someone's year in school; here, the first year of university.

0.4.n: Links the student status to 時, expressing when that status applied.

0.5.n: Means a time or period; 大学1年生の時 refers to being a university freshman.

0.6.n: Marks 時 as the time when the following event happened.

1.0.n: Refers to the university the speaker attended.

1.1.n: Links 大学 to 人たち, showing their connection to the university.

1.2.n: Combines with たち to refer to a group associated with the university.

1.3.n: Added to 人 to explicitly indicate multiple people.

1.4.n: Marks the people accompanying the speaker.

1.5.n: Pairs with に to describe doing something as a group.

1.6.n: Makes 一緒 describe how the speaker went: accompanied by other people.

1.7.n: The Japanese country name for the United Kingdom.

1.8.n: Marks イギリス as the destination of 行く.

1.9.n: The plain form directly describes 機会: an opportunity to go.

1.10.n: 行く before this noun specifies what the chance was for.

1.11.n: Marks 機会 as the thing that existed or was available.

1.12.n: Polite past form of ある; 機会がありました naturally means the speaker had an opportunity.

2.0.n: A shortened まあ, used as a conversational filler before continuing.

2.2.n: The speaker refers to himself with a commonly masculine personal pronoun.

2.3.n: Marks 僕 as the topic of the explanation continuing into the next line.

2.4.n: Combines with まで to express the period leading up to this point.

2.5.n: Sets いま as the endpoint, forming the expression up to now.

2.6.n: Names the starting school stage in the speaker's learning history.

2.7.n: Marks 小学校 as the starting point of the time span.

2.8.n: A shortened form of 高等学校, naming the final school stage mentioned.

2.9.n: Marks 高校 as the endpoint of the school years described.

3.0.n: Names the language whose grammar and vocabulary the speaker studied.

3.1.n: Connects 英語 with the grammar and vocabulary being discussed.

3.2.n: One example of what the speaker studied, paired with 単語.

3.3.n: Lists examples rather than presenting a necessarily complete list.

3.4.n: Refers to individual words learned as part of studying English.

3.5.n: Marks 文法や単語 as what the speaker studied.

3.6.n: Emphasizes study continuing over a long period.

3.7.n: 勉強する in て-form plus きた describes study continuing from the past up to the relevant point.

3.8.n: Introduces the reason for the speaker's confidence and what he told others.

4.0.n: Refers to the other people involved in the trip.

4.1.n: Marks みんな as the people the speaker addressed.

4.2.n: Adds an inclusive emphasis: the speaker told the others too.

4.5.n: A shortened まあ used as a casual filler inside the quoted speech.

4.7.n: A very casual, typically masculine pronoun that sounds more assertive than 僕 here.

4.8.n: Marks 俺 as the topic within the speaker's quoted claim.

4.9.n: Names the skill claimed; casual speech leaves out が before できる.

4.10.n: With a language name, できる expresses ability in that language, not necessarily mastery.

4.11.n: Gives the claimed English ability as the reason others should rely on him.

4.12.n: 任せる in て-form plus おいて makes a casual request to entrust matters to the speaker.

4.14.n: Casual form of という; introduces the quoted wording as an example of how he spoke.

4.15.n: Combines with っていう and に to describe the manner of speaking.

4.16.n: Makes ふう describe how he spoke rather than naming a thing.

4.17.n: Shortened 言っていました, the polite past form of 言っている, reporting what he was telling others.

0.lit: As for me, at the time of being a university first-year student,
0.tip: A noun followed by の時に means when someone was that thing.

1.lit: There was an opportunity to go to the UK together with people from university.
1.tip: A plain verb before 機会 specifies the opportunity: 行く機会 means a chance to go.

2.lit: Well, as for me, up to now, from elementary school through high school,
2.tip: から marks the starting point and まで marks the endpoint of a span.

3.lit: Because I had been studying English grammar and vocabulary all along,
3.tip: てきた shows an activity continuing from the past up to the point being discussed.

4.lit: To everyone too, I was saying something like, Well, I can use English, so leave it to me.
4.tip: っていうふうに introduces an approximate quotation: something along the lines of what the speaker said.
